name: Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy grants
summary: California state conservancy grants to nonprofits, local agencies and tribes for projects that preserve open space and habitat. Applicants consult staff first; funding is periodically authorised by the State Legislature.

eligibility.rule: If a nonprofit, qualifies under Section 501(c)(3)
Adopt contract policies increasing outreach and advertising to disadvantaged businesses and individuals
No costs outside the grant period or ordinary operating overhead like rent, mortgage, property taxes or utilities

documents: Detailed scope of work narrative with specific tasks
Project implementation timeline with completion dates for each task
Detailed description of the need for the grant
Overhead, vehicle and cell phone policies
Written justification for advance funds, if requested

calls.label: Rolling applications
calls.note: Funding is periodically authorised by the Legislature; staff discuss current opportunities in a pre-application consultation.

status.quote: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

applicant_types.quote: The Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy is pleased to assist non-profit organizations, local public agencies, and tribes by providing grant funding for projects that preserve open space and habitat

access.quote: The first step for receiving grant funding is to contact Conservancy staff for a consultation before beginning your application.

window.quote: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

effort.quote: The first step for receiving grant funding is to contact Conservancy staff for a consultation before beginning your application.
As the initial, formal step in the grant application process, the applicant shall submit a fully executed grant application form
The Budgets and Grants Officer or representative from the SMMC grants team performs initial review of grant applications
Applications will be reviewed by the Chief Staff Counsel for consistency with the Act and applicable grant requirements.
The Chief Deputy Director reviews applications for consistency with the Conservancy work program.

eligibility.quote: Eligible nonprofit organizations must qualify under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.
Applicant has adopted contract policies for the purpose of increasing outreach and advertising to disadvantaged businesses and individuals.

Examples of ineligible costs (except in rare circumstances when specifically approved in writing by the Conservancy): outside the grant performance period, indirect overhead business expenses of the grantee's fixed or ordinary operating costs such as rent, mortgage payments, property taxes or utilities

after_award.quote: Project Status Reports shall be required every quarter (Exhibit F).

Grantee agrees to permit periodic site visits by the State to determine if development work is in accordance with the approved Project Description including a final inspection upon Project completion.

documents.quote: a detailed scope of work narrative, including a list of specific tasks, a detailed budget; a timeline for project implementation (including a completion date for each task), any preliminary project plans; and a detailed description of the need for the grant

As the initial, formal step in the grant application process, the applicant shall submit a fully executed grant application form (see Exhibit A), including explanations of overhead, vehicle and cell phone policies, and a payee data record (STD 204 and 205, Exhibit B).
If the applicant requests advance funds, the applicant must provide a written justification for consideration by the Conservancy
